docs.title: Data Sourcing Workflow
docs.text:
1. Map each dashboard metric to a data source from this list.
  2. Select tier (free, paid, mixed) based on availability and budget.
  3. Automate fetching via scripts in /scripts/.
  4. Store raw data in /data/raw/{source}/{date}.csv.
  5. Process into normalized metric JSON for docs/data/dashboard.json.
  6. Audit source freshness and coverage quarterly.

Back to Top

docs.title: APIs & Automation
docs.text:
• Python packages: yfinance, sec-api, pytrends, alpha_vantage, polygon
  • Schedule: Use cron or GitHub Actions for daily/weekly refresh
  • Cache: Keep local cache to avoid rate limits
  • Error handling: Fail gracefully; flag metrics as stale

docs.title: Legal & Compliance Notes
docs.text:
• Respect Terms of Service for each source
  • Avoid scraping where prohibited
  • For investment use, retain attribution of data source
  • For public dashboards, strip proprietary fields unless licensed

docs.title: 📚 Investment Knowledge Base
docs.text:
This page is your full stock research & decision checklist. Each item maps technical term → principle → evaluation metrics → method/thresholds → signal → data sources.

Signals Legend - 🟢 Green = Strong - 🟡 Yellow = Mixed - 🔴 Red = Weak

Weights are relative (0–1) and can be tuned per strategy.

docs.title: 🔍 Research & Edge
docs.text:
Short Interest, PCR, Sentiment Divergence — Ignore the crowd (contrarian only with facts)

Evaluation metrics - Short interest % of float, put/call ratio, sentiment vs. estimate revisions Method & thresholds - Flag when negative sentiment and improving 3-month EPS estimate revisions Signal - 🟢 SI% > 10% and EPS revisions ↑; 🟡 only one condition; 🔴 neither Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - NASDAQ Short Interest, CBOE Options Data, TipRanks Analyst Revisions

Variant Perception, Edge Mapping — Own where you have a research edge

Evaluation metrics - Count of independent proprietary inputs, coverage gaps, channel checks logged Method & thresholds - Require ≥3 unique, independent inputs Signal - 🟢 ≥3; 🟡 2; 🔴 ≤1 Weight / confidence - 1.0 / 0.8 Data sources - Internal research logs, Koyfin

NPS, GRR/NRR, SLA — Best product wins

Evaluation metrics - NPS trend, churn, uptime/status incidents Method & thresholds - NPS z-score > 0.8, churn < 5% Signal - 🟢 both pass; 🟡 one; 🔴 none Weight / confidence - 0.9 / 0.7 Data sources - G2, Capterra, company status pages

Guidance Delta, Insider Sell/Buy — Don’t listen to management (verify claims)

Evaluation metrics - Guide vs. actual miss rate, insider transactions, risk language in transcripts Method & thresholds - Miss rate < 20%, sell/buy ratio < 2 Signal - 🟢 both pass; 🟡 one; 🔴 none Weight / confidence - 0.7 / 0.7 Data sources - SEC EDGAR, OpenInsider

TAM Signals, Channel Checks — Study the full value chain

Evaluation metrics - Supplier lead times, backlog, search trends Method & thresholds - Correlation with next-Q revenue > 0.5 Signal - 🟢 > 0.5; 🟡 0.3–0.5; 🔴 < 0.3 Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - Google Trends, freight indices, supplier filings

Back to Top

docs.title: 💎 Quality & Growth
docs.text:
Investment Thesis, KPIs — One-sentence thesis clarity

Evaluation metrics - Thesis clarity score, KPI coverage %, risk checklist completion Method & thresholds - LLM rubric + checklist; require ≥ 90% checklist complete Signal - 🟢 ≥90%; 🟡 70–89%; 🔴 <70% Weight / confidence - 0.4 / 0.9 Data sources - Your memo template; attach exhibits and KPI definition page

Unit Economics, Operating Leverage, ROIC — Growth quality stack

Evaluation metrics - Unit growth, pricing power, gross/operating margin expansion, reinvestment ROIC Method & thresholds - Decompose revenue bridge; unit growth > 10% and GM ↑ YoY Signal - 🟢 both; 🟡 one; 🔴 none Weight / confidence - 0.9 / 0.8 Data sources - SEC EDGAR, Yahoo Finance – Financials

Goodwill %, Organic Growth — Be wary of M&A-led growth

Evaluation metrics - % revenue from M&A, goodwill/intangibles %, integration costs Method & thresholds - Split organic vs. inorganic; goodwill/assets < 25% Signal - 🟢 <25%; 🟡 25–35%; 🔴 >35% Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.7 Data sources - 10-K/Q footnotes on acquisitions; purchase accounting notes

TAM, SAM, SOM — Brand/TAM expansion creates value

Evaluation metrics - New geo/segment revenue mix, brand extension margins Method & thresholds - Track mix shift; ≥ 10% of revenue from new TAM in last 4Q Signal - 🟢 ≥10%; 🟡 5–10%; 🔴 <5% Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - Segment disclosures; Similarweb traffic shares

Dispersion, Controversy Score — Seek a “fight” (asymmetry)

Evaluation metrics - Estimate dispersion (stdev/mean), short-reports count, bear-case map Method & thresholds - Favor high dispersion with improving revisions Signal - 🟢 both; 🟡 one; 🔴 none Weight / confidence - 0.5 / 0.5 Data sources - Consensus providers (e.g., Koyfin); public short research

Secular Beta — Ride long-term megatrends

Evaluation metrics - % revenue tied to AI/EV/Clean-energy/etc.; beta vs. theme index Method & thresholds - Map products to themes; ≥ 30% revenue to trend Signal - 🟢 ≥30%; 🟡 15–30%; 🔴 <15% Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - Theme ETFs (XLK, ICLN, etc.), industry reports

Cannibalization, Net Additive — Watch for self-cannibalization

Evaluation metrics - New vs. legacy margin mix, attach/upgrade rates, cohort ARPU Method & thresholds - Cohort analysis; net revenue additive > 0 Signal - 🟢 additive > 0; 🟡 ≈0; 🔴 negative Weight / confidence - 0.5 / 0.5 Data sources - Cohort/KPI disclosures in earnings decks

Channel Capacity — Beware hockey-stick without distribution

Evaluation metrics - Pipeline-to-rev conversion, active resellers/slots capacity Method & thresholds - Capacity supports ≥ 80% of guide Signal - 🟢 ≥80%; 🟡 60–80%; 🔴 <60% Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - Channel partner counts; distributor listings; CRM proxies

Back to Top

docs.title: 💰 Valuation & Timing
docs.text:
FCF Yield, EV/EBIT, IRR — Know intrinsic value vs. price

Evaluation metrics - DCF range, FCF yield, EV/EBIT, EV/S vs. growth, implied IRR Method & thresholds - DCF + comps band; FCFy > 5% or EV/EBIT < 12x Signal - 🟢 cheap band; 🟡 borderline; 🔴 expensive Weight / confidence - 1.0 / 0.8 Data sources - SEC EDGAR, Yahoo Finance – Statistics, Koyfin

PEG, LT Growth — High P/Es require high future growth

Evaluation metrics - PEG = P/E ÷ LT growth, reinvestment runway Method & thresholds - PEG < 1.5 preferred Signal - 🟢 <1.5; 🟡 1.5–2; 🔴 >2 Weight / confidence - 0.7 / 0.7 Data sources - Consensus estimates (broker feeds/Koyfin); price data (Yahoo)

Accretive Buyback, WACC — Buybacks accretive if E/P > after-tax cost of capital

Evaluation metrics - E/P vs. after-tax cost of debt/return on cash; buyback % of float Method & thresholds - Spread = E/P − after-tax CoD; require > 0 Signal - 🟢 positive spread; 🟡 ≈0; 🔴 negative Weight / confidence - 0.7 / 0.8 Data sources - Financials; rate data (FRED)

GM Compression — Price cuts rarely add value

Evaluation metrics - Gross-margin trend post cut; competitor response time Method & thresholds - Event study ±2 quarters; GM recovers within 2Q? Signal - 🟢 recovers; 🟡 partial; 🔴 continues down Weight / confidence - 0.4 / 0.5 Data sources - Earnings releases/decks; pricing trackers

Back to Top

docs.title: 📈 Daily Trade Signals
docs.text:
Momentum (RSI, MACD, Moving Averages) — Ride the wave

Evaluation metrics - RSI(14), MACD histogram, 20/50/200-day MA crossovers Method & thresholds - RSI < 30 = oversold; > 70 = overbought; MACD > 0 bullish Signal - 🟢 aligned bullish; 🟡 mixed; 🔴 bearish Weight / confidence - 0.7 / 0.8 Data sources - TradingView, Yahoo Finance

Volume Breakouts — Confirm price moves with volume

Evaluation metrics - Volume vs. 50-day average, VWAP Method & thresholds - Volume > 150% of average on breakout day Signal - 🟢 confirms; 🟡 weak; 🔴 absent Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.7 Data sources - Finviz, Barchart

ATR Volatility & Stop Placement — Protect capital

Evaluation metrics - Average True Range (ATR) Method & thresholds - Stop = 1–2 × ATR below entry for longs Signal - 🟢 risk defined; 🟡 loose; 🔴 undefined Weight / confidence - 0.5 / 0.8 Data sources - StockCharts

Back to Top

docs.title: 🌏 Long-Term Trend & Macro
docs.text:
Economic Indicators — Macro context matters

Evaluation metrics - GDP growth, unemployment, inflation, PMI Method & thresholds - Trend analysis: bullish if GDP↑, unemployment↓, inflation stable Signal - 🟢 all positive; 🟡 mixed; 🔴 all negative Weight / confidence - 0.8 / 0.7 Data sources - FRED, BLS

Interest Rate & Yield Curve — Watch the bond market

Evaluation metrics - 10y–2y spread, Fed funds rate Method & thresholds - Inversion = caution signal Signal - 🟢 normal; 🟡 flattening; 🔴 inverted Weight / confidence - 0.7 / 0.8 Data sources - USTreasury.gov, FRED Yield Curve

Back to Top

docs.title: 🎯 Sector & Thematic Investing
docs.text:
ETF Flows & Sector Rotation — Follow the money

Evaluation metrics - Weekly ETF inflows/outflows by sector Method & thresholds - Bullish if inflows > $500M in last week Signal - 🟢 strong inflows; 🟡 flat; 🔴 outflows Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.7 Data sources - ETF.com Flows

Thematic Tailwinds — Align with long-term megatrends

Evaluation metrics - Revenue % from AI, EV, Clean Energy, etc. Method & thresholds - ≥30% from trend theme Signal - 🟢 ≥30%; 🟡 15–30%; 🔴 <15% Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - Global X ETFs, ARK Invest

Back to Top

docs.title: 🛡️ Risk Management & Exit
docs.text:
Downside Liquidity, DSCR, Covenants — Define the bear case

Evaluation metrics - Bear-case EPS/FCF, runway, DSCR, covenant headroom Method & thresholds - Stress −20% rev, +200 bps rates; liquidity ≥ 12m runway Signal - 🟢 ≥12m; 🟡 6–12m; 🔴 <6m Weight / confidence - 0.8 / 0.7 Data sources - 10-K/Q, credit agreements (EDGAR exhibits)

Quality Short, Z-Score — Short bad businesses (not just high P/E)

Evaluation metrics - FCF < 0 persistence, leverage, deteriorating unit economics Method & thresholds - Composite “bad biz” score > 0.7 Signal - 🟢 >0.7 (candidate); 🟡 0.5–0.7; 🔴 <0.5 Weight / confidence - 0.6 / 0.6 Data sources - Financial statements (EDGAR), price data (Yahoo)

Exit Rules — Sell discipline (target hit or thesis broken)

Evaluation metrics - Price vs. target; KPI breach; stop-loss rule Method & thresholds - Alert when price ≥ target or KPI breach; enforce stop-loss Signal - 🟢 action; 🟡 watch; 🔴 hold Weight / confidence - 1.0 / 0.9 Data sources - Your memo targets; live prices (Yahoo Finance)

docs.title: The 20 Investment Principles
docs.text: A systematic approach to stock selection and portfolio management.

docs.title: 1. Ignore the crowd
docs.text:
You make money by going against the consensus.

Application: Look for stocks with low analyst coverage, negative sentiment, or recent sell-offs where fundamentals remain strong.

docs.title: 2. Always pick stocks where you feel you have a research edge
docs.text:
Your advantage comes from knowing something others don't.

Application: Focus on industries you understand deeply, companies you've researched extensively, or situations where your expertise gives you an advantage.

docs.title: 4. Don't listen to management - They are paid to be bullish
docs.text:
Management has inherent conflicts of interest.

Application: Focus on third-party data, customer reviews, competitor analysis, and independent research rather than management guidance.

docs.title: 5. Study competitors, suppliers, and customer behavior - Be a product junkie
docs.text:
The ecosystem tells the real story.

Application: Use the product, read customer reviews, analyze supplier relationships, track competitor moves, monitor industry dynamics.

docs.title: 15. When investing in growth stocks always look for a controversy ("fight")
docs.text:
Controversy creates opportunity.

Application: Seek stocks with temporary headwinds, regulatory concerns, or market misunderstandings that create temporary price dislocations.

docs.title: 3. You rarely go wrong investing in the company with the best product
docs.text:
Product superiority drives long-term success.

Application: Identify clear product leaders, assess competitive moats, evaluate customer loyalty and switching costs.

docs.title: 9. The highest quality of growth is unit growth, then pricing, then margin expansion, then cash reinvestment
docs.text:
Growth quality hierarchy matters more than growth rate.

Application: Prioritize companies growing through increased unit sales over those relying on price increases or margin expansion alone.

docs.title: 10. Be wary of companies that grow by buying other companies
docs.text:
Acquisition-driven growth is often unsustainable.

Application: Favor organic growth over M&A growth. If a company does acquire, ensure they have a strong track record of successful integrations.

docs.title: 13. Two big value creators are brand extension and TAM expansion stories
docs.text:
The best growth comes from expanding addressable markets.

Application: Look for companies successfully extending their brand into new categories or expanding their total addressable market.

docs.title: 14. High P/Es are a function of high future growth rates, and not the industry
docs.text:
Valuation should reflect individual company prospects, not sector averages.

Application: Don't avoid high P/E stocks if growth prospects justify the valuation. Focus on PEG ratios and growth sustainability.

docs.title: 6. Have in your mind what you think a stock is worth, which is different from price
docs.text:
Intrinsic value vs. market price.

Application: Develop DCF models, comparable company analysis, and sum-of-parts valuations to determine your price target independent of current market price.

docs.title: 11. Sell discipline is selling a stock once it hits your price target, or your investment thesis changes
docs.text:
Clear exit criteria prevent emotional decisions.

Application: Set price targets and thesis checkpoints before buying. Review quarterly and sell when criteria are met.

docs.title: 12. Short stocks that have bad businesses, and not because they trade at high P/Es
docs.text:
Short based on business quality, not valuation alone.

Application: Focus on companies with declining competitive positions, secular headwinds, or unsustainable business models rather than just expensive valuations.

docs.title: 19. Stock buybacks are accretive if the E/P ratio exceeds the after tax cost of debt or return on cash
docs.text:
Buybacks should create value, not just boost EPS.

Application: Calculate whether buybacks make financial sense. E/P ratio should exceed cost of capital for buybacks to be value-creating.

docs.title: 16. Buy stocks that can leverage key secular megatrends, and avoid those that will be hurt by them
docs.text:
Align with unstoppable forces.

Application: Identify major secular trends (AI, aging population, climate change) and find companies positioned to benefit while avoiding those that will be disrupted.

docs.title: 17. Always consider cannibalization of existing products when sizing up new product opportunities
docs.text:
New products may hurt existing revenue.

Application: When evaluating new product launches, assess potential cannibalization of existing products and net revenue impact.

docs.title: 18. Be wary of "hockey stick" sales forecasts absent new products or expansion to new distribution channels
docs.text:
Growth must have a catalyst.

Application: Scrutinize management projections for realistic drivers. Sustainable growth requires new products, markets, or distribution channels.

docs.title: 20. Price cuts rarely add value since competitors usually match them
docs.text:
Pricing power is crucial.

Application: Favor companies with pricing power and differentiated products over those competing primarily on price.

docs.title: 7. Be able to articulate in one sentence why you own a stock
docs.text:
Clarity of thesis is essential.

Application: Before buying, write one sentence explaining your investment thesis. If you can't, don't buy.

Template: "I own [STOCK] because [CATALYST] will drive [METRIC] leading to [OUTCOME] over [TIMEFRAME]."

docs.title: 8. Develop specific downside scenarios that would cause you to sell the stock
docs.text:
Risk management through scenario planning.

Application: Before buying, identify 3-5 specific scenarios that would invalidate your thesis and trigger a sale.

docs.title: 📊 Principle Scoring System
docs.text:
Rate each stock from 1-5 on each applicable principle:

  • 5 = Strongly Positive - Principle clearly supports the investment
  • 4 = Positive - Principle somewhat supports the investment
  • 3 = Neutral - Principle neither supports nor contradicts
  • 2 = Negative - Principle somewhat contradicts the investment
  • 1 = Strongly Negative - Principle clearly contradicts the investment

Minimum Score for Purchase: 65/100 (average of 3.25/5 across all principles) Sell Trigger: Score drops below 50/100 or any principle scores 1/5
